accuracy.evidence: Every number follows KE = ½mv²: 1 kg at 2 m/s is 2 J and 4 kg is 8 J; the 2 kg cart gives 1, 2.25, 4, 9 and 16 J at 1, 1.5, 2, 3 and 4 m/s; pairs were computed by hand (basketball 30 J v bowling ball 12 J, trolleys 40 J each, car 450 kJ v lorry 500 kJ, football 180 J v cricket ball 128 J); crash ratios (v/20)² give 1, 2.25, 4 and 9. Matches NGSS MS-PS3-1 and the KS3 energy strand.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the main error that speed affects energy the way mass does (speed prediction, 6 J and 8 J table tiles answered with 'that would mean energy grows in step with speed', challenge distractor 'Doubles'), the belief that the heavier object always has more energy (bowling ball, lorry, mastery m5), multiplying by speed once or cubing it, and thinking a parked heavy lorry has kinetic energy.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagkemv is the only lab where learners load mass blocks onto a moving cart and watch an energy bar and foam dent, drag a speed knob against a joule target, fill a speed–energy data table that plots onto a graph against a dashed in-step line, judge pairs of real moving objects, and crash-test a car at road speeds. Highest 6-token overlap with any other lab is under 10%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The relationships come from the learner's own data: 8 J needs four blocks (mass is proportional), 4 J needs only 2 m/s (speed doubled, energy ×4), and the graph only bends once they have placed 9 J and 16 J, so they see their points leave the straight dashed line. The crash bars then turn ×4 and ×9 into the road-safety reason, so evidence 1, 2 and 3 of the topic each have a hands-on step.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions before the action: twice the mass gives double, the same or four times; twice the speed gives double or four times (the classic trap); the energy–speed graph is a straight line or a steepening curve; and 60 mph against 30 mph crash energy is about 2 or 4 times. Each done message checks the choice against what the data showed.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with shuffled options, each wrong option explained: 'Only speed is squared. Mass counts once', 'Speed is squared, not cubed: 2 × 2 = 4 times', 'Mass × speed is the same, but energy uses speed squared: 8 J against 2 J', 'With no speed, it has none, however heavy it is'. Lab misses state the right calculation, e.g. speed 3 is 3 × 3 = 9 times 1 J.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation is Flesch-Kincaid grade 3.8 and adult 8.9, under the learner limits. Kinetic energy, mass, speed and joules are defined in plain words; the formula appears only in the adult text and as worked numbers in feedback, matching the proportional focus of MS-PS3-1 and leaving calculation to the separate 14–16 lesson.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph carries one relation (moving objects only, mass in step, speed squared, speed limits); the adult text names the two misconceptions, the graph slip and the 20 mph zone reasoning. Overlap with Energy Stores and Transfers and Gravitational Potential Energy is under 1%, because neither treats the mass and speed dependence.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 dark and desktop light screenshots of every step: the energy bar and target line sit above the cart, the full-width block tray and speed slider sit below the track, the table and graph share the width with five 52 px tiles underneath, pair cards fill half the width each, and four crash tiles fit one row. The longest header wraps to two lines without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: all five tasks finish with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge appears, axe-core finds no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme, and there are no console errors. Every drag has a labelled button twin (Add a 1 kg block, Faster +0.5 m/s, Put 9 joules for 3 metres per second), and every value change is spoken through the live region and the canvas aria-label.
